source_title: Bus services hit as roadways union goes on indefinite strike - The Times of India
source_excerpt: Dehradun: Public transport services across Uttarakhand faced severe disruptions on Friday as Uttaranchal Roadways Employeesâ Union launched an indefinite work boycott following the breakdown of talks with Uttarakhand Transport Corporation (UTC) management on Thursday evening.The strike, coming ahead of Diwali festive season, has triggered a deepening operational crisis for Roadways buses and prompted the state govt to intervene. Transport minister Pradeep Batra has convened a high-level meeting for Saturday afternoon at his official residence in Yamuna Colony, Dehradun, to resolve the stalemate and reach a consensus on the workersâ demands.According to an official letter issued Friday evening by UTC general manager (technical) Bhupesh Anand Kushwaha, representatives from the roadways employeesâ joint council have been invited to the 3 pm meeting. Discussions will centre on the charter of demands submitted by employee organisations, with each group instructed to send a maximum of two office-bearers.The govt-level initiative follows the failure of preliminary negotiations with corporation management. Employeesâ Union general secretary Ashok Chaudhary confirmed that no agreement could be reached on key issues, including âequal pay for equal work,â job regularisation, timely salary disbursements, and hikes in dearness allowance (DA) and honorariums for contractual and special-category staff.Chaudhary stated that the union proceeded with the work boycott from Friday as per prior notice given to management, adding that employees across all state depots would raise their voices until their demands are met.In response, UTC managing director Reena Joshi issued strict directives to all regional managers (operations and technical), reiterating a prior order dated Oct 1 that explicitly barred unauthorised leave. Terming the unionâs strike call a direct violation of corporate headquartersâ directives, the MD instructed officers to remain at their postings and ensure uninterrupted bus operations.âNevertheless, if any service is affected due to the crew (drivers and conductors), or if an employee marks their attendance in the register but subsequently joins a protest, strict action will be taken against them. Furthermore, firm action will be taken against anyone who obstructs the movement of buses from workshops or bus stations,â the MD stated in the letter, which also highlighted the financial losses suffered by the corporation during a previous boycott on Oct 23.Despite administrative warnings, passenger services were hit hard on day one. Kamal Papnai, president of the union, told TOI that several long-distance routes bound for Jaipur and Delhi were halted, while numerous services to regional destinations such as Nainital, Tanakpur, and Haridwar were cancelled, causing widespread inconvenience to festive commuters.(With inputs from Sonali Mishra in Nainital)Stay updated with the latest Dehradun news.
